items.text: The system shall prevent Autopilot activation, or promptly limit its operation, when the vehicle is outside a defined and supported operational design domain, including road types and conditions the system cannot safely handle.

The system shall detect relevant collision hazards across the vehicle’s path, including vehicles crossing or entering from the side, and shall warn and brake when needed to prevent or mitigate a collision.

The system shall monitor whether the driver is attentive and able to resume control, rather than treating steering-wheel torque alone as evidence of readiness, and shall respond to detected inattention.
If the driver does not respond to a takeover request, or the system cannot continue safely, the system shall perform a defined minimal-risk maneuver, such as slowing and stopping when feasible.
The system shall provide clear, timely indications of its operating mode, capabilities, limitations, and any conditions requiring immediate driver intervention.
The system shall adapt vehicle speed to road geometry, visibility, traffic, and detected hazards, and shall not follow the driver-set speed when doing so would be unsafe.

The system shall assess the reliability of lane and object detection and shall not continue steering or speed control based on uncertain or invalid perception without warning and transitioning to a safe state.
The system shall issue escalating, unambiguous alerts when the driver must take control, and shall allow sufficient time for a safe takeover before system capability is lost.

The system shall ensure that forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available and functioning whenever required for safe operation, or shall clearly warn the driver and restrict Autopilot use.
The system shall be designed and validated to avoid misleading drivers into believing that Autopilot can perform the full driving task or relieve them of continuous supervision.

You are a requirements engineer reviewing a safety-critical system.

Read the system description below. List the 10 most important requirements that are missing from it:
things the system should do or guarantee for safe operation that the description does not cover.
Give at most 10, ranked from most to least important.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"requirements": [{"text": "The system shall ..."}]}

System description:
# Case: Tesla Model S with Autopilot (Williston, Florida, 2016)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-17/02. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2015 Tesla Model S has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings and objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, slows down for a vehicle ahead in the same lane, and speeds up again when the lane is clear.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle centered in its lane using lane markings and the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: the system checks that the driver's hands are on the steering wheel by sensing steering torque, and shows visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users include cars, large trucks crossing or joining the road, and motorcyclists.

## Operating context
Autopilot is intended mainly for highways with limited access, in good visibility. Drivers can also turn it on for other roads, such as divided highways with cross traffic at intersections.
